title: Commuting ordinary model square for local canonical evaluation
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] on $X$ and all opens, and $K,N\in D(\mathcal O_X)$. Let $U$ be open and $P$ strictly perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex] with $K|_U\cong QP$. Write $R$ for exact restriction, $H$ for derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $D=H(K,\mathcal O_X)$, and $g$ for the canonical adjunct of $\alpha;1_N\otimes\mathrm{ev};\rho$ using the family of [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection] and the shared tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. There exist a complex $F$ representing $RN$, a chain map $f:\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,\mathcal O_U[0]))\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,F)$ with the component formula specified in [lem-pc-strictly-perfect-ordinary-evaluation], and comparison isomorphisms $a:R(N\otimes D)\cong Q\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,\mathcal O_U[0]))$ and $b:RH(K,N)\cong Q\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,F)$, such that $R(g);b= a;Q(f)$. Invertibility of $f$ is not asserted.

proof.text: Choose a complex F representing RN. Restriction commutes with Hom on opens. Transport the first variable through K|U ≅ QP.

Hom(P,F) and Hom(P,O[0]) compute local RHom. On affine subopens use the strictly-perfect Hom computation, then check the comparison quasi-isomorphism on cohomology sheaves. This yields the target comparison b on arbitrary U.

Dualizing the finite-free retractions for P makes its bounded Hom dual degreewise flat. The bounded-above flat site theorem makes this dual K-flat. Thus its tensor with arbitrary F computes the derived tensor and yields a; exact restriction commutes with the tensor model.

Define the chain map f by the component formula of ordinary evaluation using the product and coproduct universal properties. Its chain-map identity follows by expanding the Hom differential and the total differential: d_F contributes the first term, and the dual differential contributes minus (-1)^(p+q) times precomposition with d_P.

Uncurry these component maps. They agree summandwise with the representative equation for the fixed canonical tensor-Hom family. Resolve the target K-injectively; evaluation commutes with the resolution map. Localization and naturality along the representative isomorphisms give exactly R(g);b=a;Q(f). No invertibility of f is used.
